summary:
Baden-Württemberg stands under Germany's national framework, and no region-specific signal on trans visitor risk was identified in the source inventory; the national assessment applies.

Custody placement remains the sharpest documented exposure. Baden-Württemberg's own prison law retains the unrevised 1970s-era placement rules, which operate on a binary men and women housing model. A Verfassungsblog analysis of 18 March 2026 reports that placement rules in most Länder have stood unchanged since the 1970s and are now being revised: since 1 March 2026 a new Art. 17 of Rhineland-Palatinate's prison law is in force, and Bavarian, Saxon and Hamburg rules have also recently entered into force, giving a majority of Länder revised rules. Baden-Württemberg is not named among them.

The same analysis argues that no constitutional duty exists to anchor placement to the registered gender entry, since a prisoner self-declaration would intrude less on the right to gender self-determination. Only Bremen's law explicitly references the gender entry; other Länder, implicitly or not at all, do so.

How placement is applied in practice has gone both ways. A July 2026 report concerns a convicted far-right extremist holding a legally recognised female gender entry who was transferred from a women's prison to a men's prison after public outcry. The transfer indicates that placement follows the civil-registry entry and that exceptions permitting placement contrary to that entry are invoked inconsistently.
tangentialFactors: Baden-Württemberg's prison law sits within a national landscape in which a majority of Länder have recently revised their placement rules while a minority, including Baden-Württemberg, retain the 1970s-era text. A trans visitor's exposure in custody therefore depends on which Land's facilities hold them.
localsOnly: Residents held in Baden-Württemberg's prisons are subject to the Land's unrevised 1970s-era placement rules, which do not expressly reference the registered gender entry. The Verfassungsblog analysis notes that only Bremen's law explicitly references the gender entry, with other Länder doing so implicitly or not at all; Baden-Württemberg is not named in that mapping.
outOfScopeNotes: Whether Baden-Württemberg has any pending revision of its prison placement rules is unresolved in the source inventory. The inventory does not document any Baden-Württemberg-specific incident of trans prison placement, nor any Land-level guidance, complaint procedure or oversight body for trans prisoners in Baden-Württemberg.
